street_trees.name: Plant street trees on open sites
sources: City Pretty local hedonic: 3,386 Westside sales 2022-24, block fixed effects; each street tree within 50 m +0.51% (95% CI 0.24-0.79)
LAMC 62.177 in-lieu fee: $1,945 per public-works tree incl. planting and 3-yr establishment
USFS / California street-tree costing: $52-79 per tree-year upkeep

schoolyard_green.name: Green a schoolyard (asphalt to trees and grass)
sources: LAUSD 2023: $78.2M for seven campus exterior/greening packages (~$11.2M each, includes paving, fencing, ADA); LAUSD Greening Index 2022 (% green space by campus)
Crompton & Nicholls 2020 review: +8-10% adjacent to passive parks; small-park effect within ~100 m (Laszkiewicz 2022)
schoolyard_green.caveat: +1% is borrowed from passive parks; no schoolyard-specific price estimate exists.

vacant_lot_green.name: Clean and green vacant lots
sources: Lin, Jensen & Wachter 2023 (Philadelphia): +4.3% nearby after year 1
Philadelphia LandCare: $1,500 initial / $300 a year per lot (2008$)
Branas et al. 2018 RCT: gun violence -29% in poor neighborhoods
vacant_lot_green.caveat: Philadelphia costs; LA site control or land costs are not included.

community_garden.name: Community garden
sources: Voicu & Been 2008 (NYC): +1.5 pts at 1,000 ft, larger in poorer areas
Pasadena Parks Needs Assessment 2016: community garden $300k; LA RAP Hollywood rec center Phase II $16.5M + $2M contingency (2025)
community_garden.caveat: NYC effect; build cost assumed, land cost estimated.

green_alley.name: Green alley (permeable paving, trees)
sources: Avalon Green Alley North phase II (2015): $1.83M

cool_pavement.name: Cool pavement coating on hot streets
sources: Pacoima / Covina cool-pavement studies: surface -5 C, air -0.2 to -1.9 C; Middel 2020: midday radiant heat +4 C for pedestrians

pocket_park.name: Pocket park on a new lot
sources: Crompton & Nicholls 2020 review: +8-10% adjacent to passive parks; small-park effect within ~100 m (Laszkiewicz 2022)
LA 50 Parks Initiative: 5,000-20,000 sq ft parks $250k-700k to develop, land extra
Albouy, Christensen & Sarmiento-Barbieri: park value falls where homicide risk is high
pocket_park.caveat: A passive-park premium, not measured for new quarter-acre parks; land cost is estimated.

park_upgrade.name: Renovate the nearby park (new playground, paths)
sources: Livy & Klaiber 2016: playground replacement among the most capitalized park upgrades; Brasington 2023: park-maintenance levy renewal +11.6%
Culver City, Culver West Alexander playground, Nov 2025: $759,353
park_upgrade.caveat: No matched renovation coefficient; the cost covers equipment and installation.

pickleball.name: Convert a tennis court to 4 pickleball courts
sources: Redondo Beach Alta Vista 2026: tennis resurfacing + 1 court to 4 pickleball $107,408; Cerritos 2 pickleball courts $134k
Minneapolis 2014 park-facility study: passive features add value; some active/skate facilities lower nearby values

tennis.name: Build 2 public tennis courts
sources: Redondo Beach Alta Vista 2026: tennis resurfacing + 1 court to 4 pickleball $107,408; Cerritos 2 pickleball courts $134k
Minneapolis 2014 park-facility study: passive features add value; some active/skate facilities lower nearby values

basketball.name: Build a public basketball court
sources: LA County PNA 2016: one full basketball court $436,250
Minneapolis 2014 park-facility study: passive features add value; some active/skate facilities lower nearby values

dog_park.name: Dog park
sources: Castillo-Castillo et al. 2025 (Twin Cities): dog parks positively associated with nearby values (coefficient not recovered); Beverly Hills 2015 estimate $400-450k for a basic dog park
dog_park.caveat: The dog-park study's coefficient was not recovered; +0.25% is an assumption.

pool.name: Public swimming pool
sources: LA County Hilda L. Solis Aquatic Center: $36.56M revised budget (Oct 2026); LA CAO 2022: $2.08M yearly O&M for the pool program (full per-pool O&M not recovered)

splash_pad.name: Splash pad
sources: LA RAP Juntos Park splash pad: $642,021 (2017)

skate_park.name: Skate park
sources: LA County George Lane skate park (Quartz Hill): $2.1M for ~10,000 sq ft (2016); O&M not recovered
Minneapolis 2014 park-facility study: passive features add value; some active/skate facilities lower nearby values

sports_field.name: Natural-grass sports field
sources: Sunnyvale 2023: natural-grass field $516,150 vs synthetic $2.03M; Culver City PNA field replacement $2.8M

rec_center.name: Recreation center
sources: Pasadena Parks Needs Assessment 2016: community garden $300k; LA RAP Hollywood rec center Phase II $16.5M + $2M contingency (2025)

restroom.name: Park restroom and drinking fountains
sources: LA County Measure A: South LA replacement restroom building $990,000

bus_lane.name: Paint red bus-only lanes on the busy corridor
sources: Metro Wilshire bus lanes: $31.5M for 9.9 miles (2013); Culver City Robertson bus/bike lanes $1.22M (2025)
Metro Flower St bus lane: buses up to 30% faster
Beaudoin & Tyndall 2024 (Vancouver WA BRT): +5-7% home prices; Metro NoHo-Pasadena BRT $429M / 19 mi = $22.6M per mile; Vermont BRT $33.4M per mile
bus_lane.caveat: +0.5% is scaled down from full BRT; no study isolates bus lanes.

brt.name: Bus rapid transit (stations, lanes, signal priority)
sources: Beaudoin & Tyndall 2024 (Vancouver WA BRT): +5-7% home prices; Metro NoHo-Pasadena BRT $429M / 19 mi = $22.6M per mile; Vermont BRT $33.4M per mile

rail_station.name: New light rail line and station (regional project, local share)
sources: Debrezion, Pels & Rietveld 2007 meta-analysis: +4.2% residential within station area; Keeler & Stephens 2023 (LA Gold/Expo)
rail_station.caveat: Shows this area's share of a far larger regional project.

bus_shelters.name: Bus shelters with shade at busy stops
sources: LA Sidewalk & Transit Amenities Program: provisional $180,842 per shelter (city memo, 2025)

traffic_calming.name: Speed humps and traffic calming
sources: LADOT 2025: $5,958 per speed hump, up to 25-year life
Polloni 2019 (Portland): traffic calming that cuts flow 16% raises treated-street values ~1%
traffic_calming.caveat: Portland measured flow-reducing calming, not speed humps alone; hump cost is construction only.

crosswalks.name: Safer crossings (bulb-outs, ramps, refuges)
sources: Santa Monica Blvd Safety Study 2026: ADA ramp $9,000; bulb-out $11,000-18,000
FHWA: refuge islands -46% pedestrian crashes; road diets -29% crashes

road_diet.name: Road diet with protected bike lanes
sources: Metro Wilshire bus lanes: $31.5M for 9.9 miles (2013); Culver City Robertson bus/bike lanes $1.22M (2025)
FHWA: refuge islands -46% pedestrian crashes; road diets -29% crashes

sidewalks.name: Repair broken sidewalks
sources: LA Controller 2021 sidewalk audit: $51 per sq ft incl. soft costs

street_lighting.name: Brighter pedestrian street lighting
sources: Chalfin et al. (NYC RCT): street lighting -36% nighttime outdoor index crime
LA Bureau of Street Lighting: ~$5,000 per 50-ft residential lot to build; ~$90 a year upkeep assessment
Schwartz, Susin & Voicu 2003 (NYC): 1% less violent crime -> +0.116% home prices
street_lighting.caveat: The New York trial measured nighttime outdoor crime; only that share (~30%) is used.

cameras.name: Security cameras at hot spots
sources: Cameron et al. 2008 (Hollywood and Jordan Downs cameras): no significant crime effect in LA; Piza et al. 2019 meta-analysis -13% elsewhere; LA Civic Center 2024 quote ~$8,148 per camera

foot_patrol.name: Foot patrols on hot-spot blocks
sources: Ratcliffe et al. 2011 (Philadelphia RCT): foot patrol -23% violent crime; LAPD officer salary + fringe ~$159k/yr (CAO 2025)
Schwartz, Susin & Voicu 2003 (NYC): 1% less violent crime -> +0.116% home prices
foot_patrol.caveat: Chains a Philadelphia crime effect with a New York price link; cost is salary + fringe only.

violence_interruption.name: Violence interruption (GRYD-style)
sources: Brantingham, Tita & Herz 2021 (LA GRYD): violent crime ~-18% per reporting district (95% CI -3.5% to -33%; 625 districts); GRYD budget $41M/yr
Schwartz, Susin & Voicu 2003 (NYC): 1% less violent crime -> +0.116% home prices
violence_interruption.caveat: GRYD is a comprehensive strategy; its effect is assigned to a local share of program cost.

bid.name: Business improvement district (cleaning, ambassadors)
sources: MacDonald et al. 2010 (30 LA BIDs): robbery -12%
Schwartz, Susin & Voicu 2003 (NYC): 1% less violent crime -> +0.116% home prices
bid.caveat: The LA estimate is for robbery; only robbery's share of violent crime is used.

litter.name: Weekly litter and illegal-dumping cleanup
sources: MacDonald et al. 2026 street-cleaning RCT: litter -16%; LA CARE cleanup team ~$1.4M a year

graffiti.name: Fast graffiti removal
sources: No causal price effect of graffiti removal found (sourcebook round 3); Gibbons 2004 links criminal damage to prices; LA graffiti crews $11.7M / 95 crews

encampment.name: Housing-first outreach for encampments
sources: Bhandari 2024 (LA): encampments within 0.2 mi -> -1.41% sale prices; RAND Housing for Health: $30,458 per participant-year incl. county services
encampment.caveat: Assumes removing an encampment reverses the measured price discount.

blight_rehab.name: Rehab or replace blighted homes
sources: Ganduri & Maturana 2024: neighbors +2.3 pts after REO rehab; Rossi-Hansberg, Sarte & Owens 2010: $2-6 land value per $1
blight_rehab.caveat: Blighted homes inferred from Census vacancy, not identified properties.

affordable_housing.name: Affordable housing on underused land
sources: Diamond & McQuade 2019: LIHTC +6.5% within 0.1 mi in low-income areas, -2.5% in high-income; LA HHH ~$597k per unit
affordable_housing.caveat: Effects vary by neighborhood and can be negative in higher-income areas.

adu.name: Add a backyard home (ADU), owner-level
sources: Brueckner et al. 2024 (LA): ADU raises host parcel +9.2% (95% CI 6.6-11.9); Tanrisever 2025: neighbors -3% per +0.5 pt ADU density within 300 m; LA County median ADU cost $100k (2020)

solar.name: Rooftop solar, owner-level
sources: Berkeley Lab 2015: ~$4/W premium for owned solar; DOE 2025 benchmark $2.95/W installed

undergrounding.name: Underground the overhead power lines
sources: LADWP 2019: $3.4M per circuit-mile in 2024 dollars undergrounding (contracts $2.2-4.5M); CPUC Rule 20: $1.8-6.1M/mile; LADWP overhead/underground line maps (NavigateLA); CAL FIRE hazard zones
McNair & Abelson 2010 (Canberra): underground power +2.9% house prices
undergrounding.caveat: Canberra price association; private service connections and telecom work not included.

ev_hub.name: EV fast-charging hub
sources: Liang et al. 2023 (14M California sales): +3.3% within 1 km of EV chargers; CARB 2025: 8-port DC fast site $800,473; AFDC: maintenance up to $400-800 per charger-year (electricity, network extra); federal AFDC station data
ev_hub.caveat: The charger study is an association; 1% is a deep discount of its +3.3%.

microgrid.name: Solar + battery resilience hub
sources: LA County CPUC filing 2021: community microgrids $3.25-3.6M each

noise_wall.name: Freeway sound wall
sources: Moretti & Wheeler 2025: new noise barrier +6.8% within 100 m; Caltrans soundwall costs
noise_wall.caveat: OpenStreetMap maps few walls: check Caltrans before assuming a stretch is unprotected.

freeway_cap.name: Freeway cap park (regional project, local share)
sources: Klyde Warren Park cap $110M for 5 acres (2012); Hollywood Central Park proposal $250M + $780k a year
Crompton & Nicholls 2020 review: +8-10% adjacent to passive parks; small-park effect within ~100 m (Laszkiewicz 2022)
freeway_cap.caveat: Shows this area's share; full cap cost and causal effect are uncertain.

school_filters.name: Air filters in classrooms near freeways
sources: Gilraine 2020 (LA, Porter Ranch): classroom air filters raised test scores

school_bond.name: School modernization (bond-funded)
sources: Cellini, Ferreira & Rothstein 2010 (California school bonds): +6% prices; >= $1.50 home value per $1 of school capital
school_bond.caveat: Uses this area's share of a modernization; bond effects are district-wide.

library.name: Library upgrade and longer hours
sources: Gilpin, Karger & Nencka: library capital spending +21% visits; no detectable home-price change; LA Benjamin Franklin branch renovation $5.5M

clinic.name: Community health clinic
sources: Bailey & Goodman-Bacon 2015: community health centers -2% mortality 50+; Via Care East LA clinic $38.8M (25,000 sq ft)

grocery.name: Attract a full grocery store
sources: Worcester DiD: +7% within 400 m, +4% at 400-800 m after a grocery opens; Saengchote 2020: Whole Foods +6.7%
grocery.caveat: $2M is an incentive package, not the full cost of a store (private investment not counted).

main_street.name: Main-street revival (facade grants, small-business help)
sources: Ghorbani & Meltzer 2024 (NYC): more nearby retail raises 1-4 family values, lowers condo values; Teh 2007 (LA): liquor stores raise nearby crime
MacDonald et al. 2010 (30 LA BIDs): robbery -12%
main_street.caveat: A retail-density association, not a measured effect of facade grants.

outdoor_dining.name: Outdoor dining and parklets
sources: SF Controller: parklet businesses +29% revenue; LA Al Fresco corridors +$12M sales

farmers_market.name: Weekly farmers market
sources: Farmers-market studies (Maryland 2020; Edmonton 2024): positive, inverted-U with distance
farmers_market.caveat: Studies show an association with an inverted-U shape, not this exact effect.

upzone_transit.name: Allow more homes near transit (SB 79 / TOC zoning)
sources: Kuhlmann 2021 (Minneapolis): +3-5% affected single-family prices; Kestelman 2025 (LA TOC); HCD SB 79 (eff. July 2026)
upzone_transit.caveat: Policy change: public cost is planning only, so no per-dollar return is shown.

protected_bike.name: Protected bike lanes (concrete curbs)
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $1.85M per mile with concrete curbs and bike signals; MyFigueroa $20.5M / 4 mi (2018). FHWA: protected lanes cut crashes; no price study

corridor_trail.name: Trail on a power-line, rail or creek corridor
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $2.4M per mile (power-line ROW) to $4.5M (river); Immergluck 2009 (Atlanta BeltLine) found rising nearby prices, varying by area

transit_priority.name: Transit signal priority and bus bulbs
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $42,000 per signal for priority, $115,000 per bus bulb; LADOT: bus delay at signals cut ~33%

speed_cameras.name: Speed safety cameras (AB 645 pilot cities)
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $65,000 per site + $28,000/yr; FHWA / Cochrane review: large crash reductions; AB 645 pilots in LA, Long Beach, Glendale

roundabout.name: Neighborhood roundabout
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $550,000 per intersection; Retting et al. 2001: injury crashes -78% at converted intersections

ped_signals.name: Leading pedestrian signals and corner daylighting
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $8,500 per signal retiming, $1,800 per daylit corner (AB 413); Fayish & Gross 2012: pedestrian crashes reduced

school_street.name: School street (car-free at drop-off)
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $85,000 per block + $4,800/yr; London school streets: traffic and NO2 down near schools

murals.name: Public murals and art
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $35,000 per 1,000 sq ft mural; LA Mural Ordinance registry; no causal price study

tiny_forest.name: Miyawaki tiny forest
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $65,000 per 0.1-acre site + $8,500/yr; no price study

fiber_5g.name: Fiber to the home and 5G small cells
sources: Cost from a Gemini research pass, unverified (re-audit kept the figure but quoted no source); $3,200 per home passed (fiber); no causal price study for small cells (earlier cited study was fabricated)

W: Regional 50% via 110-point scoring, 60 to qualify; Municipal 40% goes straight to cities for green streets
A: competitive grants, priority for high park-need areas
M: local return to every city plus capital programs
SS4A: Safe Streets and Roads for All
TCC: state cap-and-trade, whole-neighborhood plans in top-25% CalEnviroScreen areas
AHSC: state cap-and-trade: housing plus transit/bike/walk projects
CFC: sell verified urban-tree carbon credits to fund upkeep
P4: $10B state bond: water, heat, parks, wildfire
R20: phasing out: only banked credits remain (no new credits after 2022)
IRA: cash refund of 30%+ on public solar, batteries and chargers
NEVI: federal formula funds for fast chargers near freeways
EPA: assessment and cleanup of contaminated land
ULA: ~$215M a year for affordable housing and acquisition
STAP: ad concession pays for shelters and upkeep
EIFD: captures future property-tax growth; see the calculator
BID: property-owner assessment for cleaning and safety
CDBG: federal block grant for lower-income areas
